audit.whatIsWrong: Six strings call Tactical Sweep a 'true-damage cone' and treat Precision Protocol as an ordinary auto proc. The true damage is on the Q, not the W.
audit.why: Riot's Tactical Sweep text: a delayed cone where 'enemies in the outer half are slowed and take extra damage, while also healing Camille' — no true damage, but a heal the page never mentions. Riot's Precision Protocol is the recastable attack modifier and the kit flags it as the true-damage source and an auto reset. Playing around the wrong ability means eating the heal and mistiming the burst.
audit.corrected: True damage reassigned to Precision Protocol; Tactical Sweep described as the delayed cone whose outer half slows and heals her.

audit.whatIsWrong: Hookshot's knockup cancelling Aegis Assault is never stated, and neither is Hookshot's terrain requirement.
audit.why: Riot's Hookshot text: 'Camille pulls herself to a wall, leaping off and knocking up enemy champions upon landing.' Aegis Assault is a channel any CC ends. So her engage both denies your one damage-proof button and cannot happen at all in open lane. _missing-interactions.json flags the channel break.
audit.corrected: Fight away from walls; never start the channel while Hookshot's 16s is up.

audit.whatIsWrong: Adaptive Defenses is never named, so nothing tells you why the tail of your burst disappears.
audit.why: Riot's text: her basic attacks on champions grant a shield 'equal to a percentage of Camille's maximum health against their damage type'. Pantheon is physical, so every auto she lands on you puts a percent-max-HP physical shield in the way — and it scales with her HP, not her damage.
audit.corrected: Adaptive Defenses now named in the 2-item spike as the reason your physical burst stops landing.

audit.why: EVEN 6/10 fits 50.54% over 920 games. Levels 1-3 are Pantheon's because Hookshot does not exist yet; 4-6 is skill; the side lane is Camille's at carry threat 9/10.

audit.whatIsWrong: Not one cooldown appears anywhere — the coverage report flags 'NO cooldown-sequencing advice'.
audit.why: Hookshot 16/15/14/13/12, Precision Protocol 9/8/7/6/5, Tactical Sweep 15/14/13/12/11, The Hextech Ultimatum 140/115/90, against Shield Vault's 13s and Aegis Assault's 22s. Hookshot at 16s versus your 13s W is the sequencing rule the page was missing.
audit.corrected: Real numbers added to the spikes, the cooldown block, the dos and the interactions row.

audit.whatIsWrong: Camille is 'him'/'his' in three strings, and dontsFull[1] is titled 'Fight near walls' with a body about burning a cooldown.
audit.why: Boilerplate left unedited; the walls entry is the single most important don't in the matchup and said nothing.
audit.corrected: Pronouns fixed and the walls body rewritten to Hookshot's terrain requirement.

edits.before: Camille is the rare duelist who is genuinely beatable at levels 1-3, so press it. At level 1 your point-and-click W stun plus a Q tap is a real all-in and she has no E hookshot yet to dash out of it. Bait or simply ignore her early aggression — her W true-damage cone and Q proc need item stats to hurt, and you can angle your E block to eat the cone outright. Land the stun, weave the empowered Q, and trade her down before she stabilizes.
edits.after: Camille is the rare duelist genuinely beatable at levels 1-3, so press it. At level 1 Shield Vault dashes 600 onto her with a stun and she has no Hookshot to leave with. Her Tactical Sweep cone and Precision Protocol need item stats to hurt, and facing her lets Aegis Assault eat the cone outright — just do not let the outer half land, because that half heals her. Land the stun, weave the empowered Q, trade her down.

edits.before: Through levels 4-5 you still control it: held-Q poke chips her and your E block shuts off her W cone and the empowered Q she wants to land in every trade. Keep forcing short W-stun trades and reset. At 6 the lane flips — her R cages you into a clean 1v1 where her W heal and Q true damage start winning the exchange, so do not get caught alone walking up. Bank your tempo into Grand Starfall roams instead of dueling her past 6.
edits.after: Through levels 4-5 you still control it: held-Q poke chips her and facing her blanks Tactical Sweep and the Precision Protocol auto. Force short W-stun trades in open lane — Hookshot needs terrain, and its knockup ends an Aegis Assault channel outright, so never start the channel with her 16s E up. At 6 The Hextech Ultimatum cages you for a 1v1 she wins; bank your tempo into Grand Starfall roams instead.

notes: _missing-interactions.json makes two claims about The Hextech Ultimatum I did not write. It says the R is a channel that Shield Vault cancels outright, and separately that Camille goes untargetable through it. Riot's own text is 'Camille dashes to target champion, anchoring them to the area' plus bonus magic damage on her attacks — no channel, no untargetability. Both look like tooltip-parse misfires on the kit's flags, so they are logged in unverified rather than shipped. The verified channel-breaker is Hookshot's landing knockup, which is in Riot's text and is now on the page.
